matter: A petition against deletions in Maharashtra's revision, W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026. The Court issued notice to the Election Commission on 26 October.
due: The petition is listed for hearing. On 26 October the Court declined to extend the time for claims and objections or to stop the final roll before hearing the Commission.
quote: A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana heard Writ Petition (Civil) No. 1330 of 2026 on October 26, 2026, and listed it for November 5, 2026.

matter: The petitions alleging that decisions of the Election Commission, those on the revision among them, were taken without the agreement of the two Election Commissioners, led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026.
due: The lead petition is listed for admission as item 26 in the Chief Justice's court, before the Chief Justice, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana. The court sits from 10:30 am. Seven connected petitions are listed with it, among them the petitions of Asaduddin Owaisi, of Rahul Gandhi and others, of Digvijaya Singh and of Dola Sen.

matter: The petition of two transparency activists on Delhi's revision, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, and an application they were told to file on the Commission's letter about Form 6.
due: The petition is listed for admission as item 26 in the Chief Justice's court, before the Chief Justice, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana, with an application for clarification or direction and an intervention application. A connected petition, W.P.(C) No. 1339 of 2026, is listed with it as item 26.1. matter: A petition by a group of advocates for guidelines on processions and protests near the Supreme Court, after the Opposition's march of 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner.
due: On 3 November the Court sought replies from Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and the Centre, and the Centre said it would reply by this date.
quote: Posting the matter for November 23, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant also sought the Centre’s response to the petition

matter: Petitions on Kerala's revision, heard with the matters on Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
due: On 30 October the Election Commission was given four weeks to file its counter affidavit and to answer the points in the petitioners' note.
quote: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने चुनाव आयोग को जवाबी हलफनामा दाखिल करने के लिए चार सप्ताह का समय दिया है।

matter: The petitions on the restrictions imposed during the protests against the Chief Election Commissioner in October, led by MA Baby v. Union of India, with which the Court will hear the petition of two traders' associations on their business losses and on Ramlila Maidan as a protest site, W.P.(C) No. 1395 of 2026.
due: The petitions are tentatively listed for hearing. On 18 November the Court issued notice on the traders' petition to the Cockroach Janta Party, the Congress, the Aam Aadmi Party and the All India Students' Association, and said it would be heard with these petitions.
quote: The bench stated that the traders' petition can be posted along with the other petitions (MA Baby v Union of India and connected matters) which question the restrictions imposed by the authorities in the wake of protests. Those matters are tentatively listed on November 27.

matter: Petitions against the exclusion of electors in Maharashtra's revision. The Election Commission asked for them to be deferred because the Supreme Court is hearing the revision.
due: The petitions are listed for hearing. The High Court has given no view on their merits.
quote: The Bombay High Court has fixed December 1 for hearing petitions that challenge alleged arbitrary exclusions of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra, after the Election Commission of India (ECI) sought a deferral

matter: The application of Kumud Gangwar, a former state general secretary of the Congress, under section 173(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita against the former District Election Officer of Pilibhit, Gyanendra Singh, and six others, over the alleged changes to the roll of Pilibhit Sadar.
due: The District Magistrate's inquiry report and the station house officer's report are due by this date, the next date in the case. The magistrate, Mangal Dev Singh, registered the application as a miscellaneous case on 18 November and issued notices to the seven named. He sought a report on the former District Election Officer from the divisional commissioner, directed the District Magistrate of Pilibhit to hold a preliminary inquiry into the other public servants named and report, and asked the station house officer to report whether any case has been registered in the matter.
quote: For the other public servant opposite parties, the district magistrate, Pilibhit, has been directed to conduct a preliminary inquiry into the facts mentioned in the application and ensure submission of the inquiry report to the court by the next date of December 2, 2026.

matter: The petition of two transparency activists on Delhi's revision, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026.
due: On 19 November the Court asked the Election Commission to give the number of enumeration forms filled and of Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 applications made. It said it would then take stock and consider whether to extend the deadline for electors left off the draft roll.
quote: On December 2, we can take stock of the progress made by this purported deadline.

court: Court of the First Additional Sessions Judge
matter: A revision petition by the Banbhoolpura police against a Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over Form 7s filed to delete 28 electors in the name of a booth level agent who says he did not file them. On 30 October the court refused to stay the order.
due: The revision petition is listed for hearing.
quote: स्थगन अर्जी खारिज करने के साथ पुनरीक्षण याचिका पर अगली सुनवाई के लिए सात दिसंबर 2026 की तारीख तय की गई है।

matter: The petitions alleging that decisions of the Election Commission, those on the revision among them, were taken without the agreement of the two Election Commissioners, led by W.P.(C) No. 1246 of 2026, with the application by Rahul Gandhi and ten other opposition leaders to put 48 written questions to the Commission.
due: The petitions are listed for hearing. On 17 November the Court said it would hear the matter after the Election Commission files its objections to the application for the 48 questions.
quote: A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that the matter will be heard on December 9 after the ECI files its objections to the plea.

matter: Petitions by the RJD Member of Parliament Manoj Jha and an advocate challenging section 16 of the Act of 2023 on the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners, which bars civil and criminal proceedings against them for their official acts. The Court issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission on 4 November.
due: The petitions are listed for hearing.
quote: The court listed the petitions on December 18.
